title: How Does GoLinks Use AI in 2026?
summary: Learn how GoLinks uses AI, from its newest feature AI-suggested go link names and descriptions, to semantic search and Not Found suggestions.
body_markdown:
Go links are meant to be fast: type a short, memorable go link and land exactly where you need to be. AI plays a role in making that work, across three parts of the GoLinks experience. It helps people find the right go link even when they don’t know the exact name, it steps in when someone lands on a link that doesn’t exist, and it now helps people create better-named go links from the start.


**Quick answer:** As of 2026, GoLinks uses AI in three ways. AI-powered search surfaces the right go link based on meaning, not just an exact name match. AI-powered Not Found suggestions point people toward the right link when they land on one that doesn’t exist. And AI-suggested naming generates a go link name and description automatically when someone creates a new link through the GoLinks extension. Together, these cover a go link from the moment it’s created through everyday, real-world search behavior.


## AI-Powered Search and Semantic Matching


GoLinks uses AI to power search across an organization’s go link library. That search is built around meaning rather than exact text, so it doesn’t just match a search term to an identical go link name. If someone types something close to the right name or searches using different words than whoever created the link, GoLinks can still surface the go link they’re actually looking for, as well as an AI summary in response.


In a larger organization with hundreds or thousands of go links, it’s nearly impossible to remember the exact name of every link, and naming conventions inevitably vary between the people who created them. Semantic, AI-powered search closes that gap, so people can search the way they’d naturally think, rather than needing to recall an exact name.

## AI-Powered Not Found Suggestions


Sometimes someone lands on a go link that doesn’t exist, whether because of a typo or a guess that didn’t quite match how the link was named. Instead of a dead end, GoLinks uses AI on the Not Found page to suggest likely matches from the organization’s go link library. Because the matching is semantic, it works even when the attempted name is only loosely related to the actual go link, not just when it’s a near-identical typo.


This keeps a wrong guess from turning into a wasted trip back to searching in the dashboard or sending a message to a coworker. These moments happen often enough across an organization that this adds up to real time saved.


## AI-Suggested Go Link Names and Descriptions


The newest place AI shows up in GoLinks is link creation itself. The GoLinks browser extension already auto-populates the destination URL when someone creates a go link. Now it also reads the page and suggests a go link name and description to go with it, so the person creating the link isn’t starting from a blank field.


When someone opens the GoLinks extension on a page, whether it’s a Figma board, a Jira project, a GitHub repo, or an internal resource, GoLinks reads the page content and generates a suggested go link name and a short description based on it. From there, the person creating the link can use the suggestion as-is, edit it, or hit regenerate for a different option, then create the go link in a single click.


For example, a Figma board titled “GoSearch Enterprise Onboarding Q3 2026” gets a suggested link like **go/q3-ent-onboarding** , along with a description summarizing what the board contains. A Jira board called “GoLinks Marketing” gets suggested as **go/mktg-board** . In both cases, the person creating the link doesn’t have to stop and think through naming conventions or write a description themselves.


## How AI Improves GoLinks


Go links work best when people can guess or search their way to the right one, which is exactly what AI-powered search and Not Found suggestions are built to support. AI-suggested naming supports that goal from the other direction: it gives every link creator a consistent starting point, drawing on common naming patterns so links stay easy to find as a library grows. The automatic description is often the first thing people skip when creating a link quickly, even though it’s what makes a link understandable to teammates who come across it later.


**Benefits by team:**


- **IT and knowledge management teams:** consistent naming patterns across a growing go link library.
- **Marketing and sales teams:** faster link creation for campaign pages, decks, and shared assets.
- **New hires and cross-functional teams:** predictable, guessable go link names that make internal resources easy to find.
- **Admins:** stronger link hygiene, since descriptions are populated automatically instead of left blank.

## Frequently Asked Questions


****How does GoLinks use AI?****


GoLinks uses AI in three ways: to power semantic search across an organization’s go link library, to suggest likely matches on the Not Found page when someone lands on a link that doesn’t exist, and to suggest a go link name and description when a new link is created. Together they help people find, recover, and create go links faster.


****Does GoLinks’ AI search only work with exact go link names?****


No. GoLinks’ search is semantic, meaning it matches based on meaning rather than requiring an exact text match. A close guess or a search phrased differently than the original go link name can still surface the right result.


****What happens if I land on a go link that doesn’t exist?****


GoLinks’ Not Found page uses AI to suggest likely matches from your organization’s go link library, based on semantic similarity to what you typed. This works whether the mismatch is a small typo or a guess that only loosely resembles the actual link name.


****Does AI-suggested naming work on any webpage** ?**


Yes. The GoLinks extension can suggest a name and description for any page you’re on when you open it, including tools like Figma, Jira, GitHub, and internal wikis. The destination URL is captured automatically, so the suggestion is generated from the actual page content rather than a generic template.


****Can I edit the AI-suggested name before creating t** he go link?**


Yes. The suggested name and description are fully editable. You can change them, use the regenerate option for a new suggestion, or leave them as-is and create the go link in one click.
